results.checks: A stray_oca_soak row exists in which the sweep GRADED a non-keyed protective group as a stray (`decision: stray_unkeyed`) AND actually cancelled it (`acted: true`) rather than being held back by PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS. Those are two different facts and both are required: `acted` is the EFFECT, `decision` is the finding, and a row carrying the finding at `mode: annotate` is the STAGED state, not a cancel. The positive control (`decision` present with any of its three values) is what separates 'the sweep ran and found no strays' from 'the log is absent or unreadable' — without it an empty log emits a confident negative, which is the state this row has been in since 2026-08-26.

The soak records `cancel_calls_made` and a `verify_state`, but `BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT` is exactly the defect of trusting a self-report, so the confirming read is /api/diag/ib_open_orders on a FRESH client (that route's own view is monotonically stale, BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW). It also cannot see whether the cancelled group was genuinely this trade's abandoned protection rather than something a human placed — `ungrouped` is refused for that reason and `stray_unkeyed` is an inference from the group NAME.

This looks for a CLOSED trade that is real-money, on one of the nine shipped e35 legs, whose pnlProvenance is measured or estimated (clears_when explicitly rules out fabricated and unverified), and — the word clears_when calls 'the whole criterion' — OPENED AFTER the deploy rather than merely closed after it. The boundary 2026-08-30T14:05:00+00:00 is not the commit time: it is the instant the observation records half (a) as MEASURED true on the running trader, so a matching trade demonstrably opened under config confirmed live. It is conservative by construction — it may exclude a qualifying trade opened slightly earlier, which errs toward under-reporting, the safe direction for a criterion that must not be cleared spuriously. `openedAt` is compared lexicographically, which is chronological ONLY because the route serves a +00:00 offset (measured); a switch to a 'Z' suffix would silently break it, and the positive control is what would catch that. results.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that the trade was closed BY THE STRATEGY. clears_when forbids grading the exit off exit_reason alone, and the row's own near-miss is the proof: trade 4904 read 'reconciler_filled' for what was an OPERATOR FLATTEN. No field on this route separates a strategy exit from an operator action, so that judgement stays a session's. Nor does a pass establish BROKER TRUTH, which clears_when asks for: pnlProvenance grades how THIS ROW's number was derived, while journalTrust grades whether the ACCOUNT reconciles with the venue wallet at all, and they are different questions — a 'measured' row on a 'known_divergent' account is exactly that gap, and bybit_2 is such an account. Finally it cannot tell whether the trade exercised the CHANGED geometry: a trade on ada_pullback_2h or trend_donchian_xrp_4h that closed on its stop says nothing about the tp_r 50->3/4 change those two legs received, which is the part of the ship the row most wants looked at. It reads /api/bot/trades/closed, which carries no entry/sl geometry, so it cannot compute cap_r = 0.099*entry/risk and therefore cannot tell whether the DECLARED tp_r or the VENUE CLAMP set that trade's target. It returned `pass` on 2026-09-01T05:38:50Z — correctly, on trade 5250 — and that trade is clamp-bound (cap_r 2.892634 < tp_r 3) and does NOT satisfy (b). So this probe is now a PRE-FILTER: a `fail` still means no candidate exists at all, which is useful and honest, but a `pass` means only 'a candidate passed the clauses I can see' and a session must then check cap_r against that leg's tp_r from the order package before grading. results.checks: Looks for a gpu-burst-train.yml run whose logs carry the preflight step at all, over the last 20 runs. ⚠️ THE REASON THIS ROW CARRIED FOR HAVING NO PROBE WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, which is why it now has one: it said a scheduled probe 'cannot produce that without FIRING a GPU job, which spends real budget'. True about FIRING and irrelevant to PROBING — NO probe in this family produces the event it watches (pairs_soak does not open a pair; arbitration_fanout_soak does not route an order). Conflating producing an observation with observing it turned a buildable probe into a declared impossibility. This fires no job, spends nothing, and only reads.
results.is_not: ⚠️ A PASS HERE IS THE WEAKEST IN THE FAMILY AND MUST NOT CLEAR THE ROW ON ITS OWN. clears_when demands the preflight be OBSERVED MAKING A DECISION — refusing on budget or admitting — and explicitly rules out a dry run. This cannot separate those: with GPU_BURST_ARMED != 1 the workflow runs a DRY PREFLIGHT ONLY, and its log carries the same step name as an armed run. So a pass means 'a run exists that reached the preflight step', and a session must read that run's own output to see whether it was armed and what it decided. The literal is deliberately the step name rather than a decision string, because no decision string has ever been observed in a real run — inventing one would be a predicate matching nothing while looking precise. Tighten it to the real decision line the first time an armed run happens. Since the event never occurs spontaneously, a FAIL here means 'nobody has fired one', not 'the gate is broken'.

results.checks: BOTH halves, in the two DIFFERENT workflows that print them, because clears_when requires both and a pass on one half is the over-read this family exists to prevent. (a) `session-brief: verdict=inherited` in a guards.yml run — emitted only by render_session_brief.py's inherited branch, so its presence IS the diff-scoping path having been taken on a real PR. The positive control `session-brief:` appears in essentially every guards run, so a workflow rename, an expired log or a revoked token becomes could_not_look instead of a permanent quiet negative.
